name: The Jesus Lizard
label: Touch and Go
lede: Two refugees from Austin's noisiest band, a guitarist who never played a random note and a singer who spent half of every show on top of the audience: four Albini records, one arrest, one bad major-label deal and a comeback album 26 years later.

eras.title: A lizard that runs on water
eras.text: Scratch Acid had just broken up in Austin when guitarist Duane Denison went looking for a singer. He got David Yow and bassist David Wm. Sims, a drum machine, and a name borrowed from the basilisk, the lizard that can run across water. By 1989 all three were in Chicago, in Steve Albini's orbit and on Touch and Go.

years.h: Duane Denison recruits David Yow and David Wm. Sims
years.p: In Austin, guitarist Duane Denison asks ex-[[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]] singer David Yow to sing, with David Wm. Sims on bass. The trio rehearses with a drum machine and names itself after the Jesus lizard, a basilisk that runs on water.

years.h: David Yow and David Wm. Sims move to Chicago
years.p: David Yow and David Wm. Sims relocate to Chicago in 1988, where Sims is playing in [[Rapeman|899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af]] with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] and [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]]. Duane Denison follows in 1989.

years.h: Pure EP, the Jesus Lizard's debut · Touch and Go
years.p: Recorded with Steve Albini, Pure is the only Jesus Lizard release built on a drum machine. It starts a run on Touch and Go that lasts through 1994.

years.h: Mac McNeilly's first show as the Jesus Lizard's drummer
years.p: Drummer Mac McNeilly, from Phantom 309, plays his first Jesus Lizard show on July 1, 1989, replacing the drum machine for good.
years.xp: Duane Denison told Guitar World that all four lived together in a three-bedroom apartment on Chicago's west side, around each other around the clock. He also said the band's arguments sometimes came to punches, shoving and thrown lamps.

eras.title: Four records with Albini
eras.text: Steve Albini recorded four straight Jesus Lizard albums, with Yow's voice buried low in the mix like one more instrument. Onstage Yow leapt into crowds, stripped, licked and climbed on people, and the shows became as famous as the records.

years.h: Head, the Jesus Lizard's first album · Touch and Go
years.p: The Jesus Lizard's first full-length, and the first of four in a row recorded by Steve Albini.

years.h: David Yow's stage act: into the crowd, out of his clothes
years.p: David Yow sings from on top of the audience, strips, licks people and chats with the crowd mid-song. Michael Azerrad compared his voice to a kidnap victim howling through duct tape.
years.xp: Yow calls himself a vocal stylist, not a singer, and described the band as four white guys playing a cross between [[Led Zeppelin|678d88b2-87b0-403b-b63d-5da7465aecc3]] and [[The Birthday Party|cbcd4d49-e892-4fc6-a313-35f275a153d2]]. Mac McNeilly rejected the noise-rock label: to him it was rock music, full stop.

years.h: Goat, the Jesus Lizard's second Albini album
years.p: Goat and its follow-up Liar are the two records critics hold up as landmarks of early-'90s noise rock. Mouth Breather and Seasick are here.

years.h: Liar: Boilermaker, Gladiator and Puss
years.p: The Jesus Lizard's third album with Steve Albini, including Puss, the song that would share a single with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]].

years.h: A split single with Nirvana reaches No. 12 in the UK
years.p: Touch and Go pairs the Jesus Lizard's Puss with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s Oh, the Guilt. According to Wikipedia it reached No. 12 on the UK singles chart.

years.h: Lash EP · Touch and Go
years.p: A stopgap EP between Liar and Down.

years.h: Down, the last Albini album and last on Touch and Go
years.p: The fourth Jesus Lizard album with Steve Albini closes the Touch and Go years. The live album Show follows the same year.

eras.title: Capitol, and the long way down
eras.text: The Jesus Lizard signed to Capitol, played Lollapalooza and lost part of its audience on the first major-label record. A drummer left, then another, and Capitol dropped the band in the middle of its contract.

q: Become a third-string act for a big corporation
years.h: The Jesus Lizard leaves Touch and Go for Capitol Records
years.p: The Jesus Lizard signs with Capitol in 1995 and records Panic in Cicero for the Clerks soundtrack. Steve Albini, their longtime engineer, thought it was a terrible mistake.
years.xp:
Albini called the Jesus Lizard the best band of the '90s, hands down, and said the Capitol deal doomed them to be a minor act for a corporation that didn't care about them or their fans.

Duane Denison's own verdict, to Guitar World: half the people who bought Down didn't buy the Capitol album, and he thought the Capitol album was better.

years.h: David Yow arrested at Lollapalooza in Cincinnati
years.p: At Riverbend Music Center, David Yow exposes himself onstage, he said as a protest against censorship of the city's Mapplethorpe exhibit. Police cuff him after the set; he's held about six hours and fined $327.
years.xp: Cincinnati CityBeat reports Yow was also banned from Hamilton County for a year. When police handed him paperwork to sign, he wrote an insult to them across it and signed his name.

years.h: Shot, the first Capitol album, produced by Garth Richardson
years.p: The Jesus Lizard's first record without Steve Albini. Duane Denison says half the fans who bought Down skipped Shot, and that Shot was the better album.

years.h: Mac McNeilly quits; Jim Kimball of Mule takes over
years.p: Mac McNeilly leaves at the end of 1996, worn out by touring and wanting time with his family. Jim Kimball of [[Mule|84189509-850d-428b-a8f0-1626cb0eabb3]] and the Denison/Kimball Trio replaces him.

years.h: An EP with Andy Gill, John Cale and Jim O'Rourke
years.p: The self-titled Jesus Lizard EP on Jetset has tracks produced by [[Gang of Four|d8661c02-f423-4d72-8044-40ff05daf7a1]]'s [[Andy Gill|eb3f978d-272a-460d-bc3e-a1a82ecb8147]], [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] and [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]].

years.h: Jim Kimball leaves; Brendan Murphy is drummer number three
years.p: Jim Kimball leaves in August 1998. Brendan Murphy, from the [[Wesley Willis Fiasco|fc7242e2-e873-4a99-9654-5cf2caa50870]], takes over.

years.h: Blue, the Jesus Lizard's last Capitol album
years.p: Produced by [[Andy Gill|eb3f978d-272a-460d-bc3e-a1a82ecb8147]], Blue is the band's most experimental record and its last for 26 years.

q: We did it. We said everything we wanted to say.
years.h: Last show in Umeå, Sweden, then the Jesus Lizard splits
years.p: Dropped by Capitol mid-contract, the Jesus Lizard plays its last show at Sweden's Umeå Open festival and announces the breakup in June 1999.

eras.title: Accountant, actor, Tomahawk
eras.text: The band scattered into very different lives until Touch and Go's reissue plans and a 20th anniversary pulled them back. The first reunion ran two years and was supposed to be the last.

years.h: Bang collects the Jesus Lizard's singles and rarities
years.p: Touch and Go releases Bang, a compilation of 7-inch tracks and oddities.

years.h: Where the Jesus Lizard went: LA, New York, Tomahawk
years.p: Duane Denison plays in [[Tomahawk|947911f8-60bc-44ab-9782-f97020f15b43]] with [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]]. David Yow moves to Los Angeles for graphic design and acting, David Wm. Sims becomes an accountant in New York, and Mac McNeilly plays in Mouse with his wife.

years.h: David Yow and David Wm. Sims reunite Scratch Acid
years.p: Yow and Sims play with [[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]] again, with [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]] and [[Brett Bradford|70ab1b12-492b-4031-bccd-c7e402d88353]], for Touch and Go's 25th anniversary festival in Chicago.

years.h: The Jesus Lizard reunites with Mac McNeilly
years.p: The classic line-up returns and plays Chicago's Pitchfork Music Festival and All Tomorrow's Parties in England and New York. On October 6, Touch and Go reissues every studio album, remastered by Steve Albini and Bob Weston.

years.h: Club: a 2009 Nashville show on DVD and double LP
years.p: MVD releases Club, filmed at Exit/In in Nashville in 2009. The members say this reunion was probably their last.

years.h: David Yow's solo album, 15 years in the making
years.p: David Yow releases Tonight You Look Like a Spider on Joyful Noise. In October the band cancels a planned All Tomorrow's Parties appearance in Melbourne.

years.h: The Jesus Lizard Book, by the band
years.p: The four members put together their own history in The Jesus Lizard Book, with photos, flyers and their own stories.

eras.title: Twenty-six years between albums
eras.text: The second reunion stuck. After years of touring on the old songs, the Jesus Lizard made its first album since 1998, on Mike Patton's label.

years.h: The Jesus Lizard's first tour in eight years
years.p: Announced in September 2017, the second reunion starts with a December tour. Riot Fest in Chicago follows in 2018.

years.h: Steve Albini, who recorded Pure through Down, dies at 61
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] dies of a heart attack. He recorded Pure, Head, Goat, Liar and Down, and called the Jesus Lizard the best band of the '90s.

years.h: Rack, the Jesus Lizard's first album in 26 years
years.p: The Yow, Denison, Sims and McNeilly line-up releases Rack on [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]]'s Ipecac Recordings, led by the single Hide and Seek, and tours the US and UK to strong reviews.
